cards.name: Line Styles
cards.summary: Line Style Library (the install's linestyles.dot, read for facts): 27 dash patterns for outlines, numbered 1 to 27 in the Outline style list. The thumbnail is a swatch strip drawn from the file's dash data, not a script render of the styles in CorelDRAW: 27 thin black dashed lines stacked on neutral grey, from a tight dotted line at the top to long dashes, then dash-and-dot rows, then irregular multi-dash patterns. Rows 1-12 repeat one dash of length 1, 2, 5 or 10 with gaps of 1, 3 and 5; rows 13-18 pair a long dash (5) with short dots (1); rows 19-27 mix dashes of 1, 4, 5 and 10 with wide gaps.
use_for: dotted and dashed borders on labels, coupons and tickets
cut, fold and perforation lines on dielines and packaging
map routes, chart gridlines and technical drawings
avoid: Expecting exact lengths: the file stores plain numbers (1, 2, 5, 10), not millimetres, and the dashes appear to scale with the outline width, so check the look at the real stroke width.
Looking for a style by name: the entries are numbered 1 to 27 and have no names.
Cutter or plotter jobs that need dash lengths in millimetres: draw the dashes as objects or set the machine's own line type.
cards.applies_to: the outline (stroke) of a curve, shape, text or any other object that has an outline; it sets the dash pattern and leaves width and colour alone
cards.how_to_apply: Select the object, then pick a pattern from the outline Style picker (the line-style list on the property bar or in Object Properties > Outline). Script: shape.Outline.Style = Application.OutlineStyles.Item(i), with i from 1 to 27 (base 1; the harvest read the list live and found the same 27 patterns as the file Draw/linestyles.dot in the install). Width is set separately with shape.Outline.Width.

verified.note: Swatch strip: 27 thin black dash rows on light grey, dotted at the top to long dashes, dash-dot rows, then sparse mixed patterns; the 27 patterns decoded from linestyles.dot match the card.

cards.name: A0
cards.summary: New Document preset (Print category): the ISO A0 sheet, the largest of the A series. It starts a document with a portrait page 841 x 1189 mm (33.1 x 46.8 in), CMYK primary colour mode, 300 dpi rendering resolution and Enhanced view. avoid: Detailed raster effects at full size: at 300 dpi this page is about 9,900 x 14,000 px, so shadows and transparencies make very heavy files; design at a smaller scale and enlarge if your printer accepts it.

cards.name: Double
cards.summary: New Document preset (Print category): a double-size US sheet, 11 x 17 in (the same page size as Tabloid). It starts a document with a portrait page 11 x 17 in (279 x 432 mm), CMYK primary colour mode, 300 dpi rendering resolution and Enhanced view. It sets the page up only and has no look of its own; read from the install's PaperTypes.xml and DocDestinations.xml.
use_for: two Letter pages laid out as one sheet
avoid: Looking for a different size from Tabloid: the stored size is identical.
Screen or web output: this preset is CMYK at 300 dpi; start from Default RGB or a Web preset for screen work.
Printing without checking colour and bleed: the preset stores CMYK with the U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2 profile and no bleed value, so set the profile and bleed your printer asks for.
cards.applies_to: the document being created, not an object: choosing the preset in File > New sets the first page's size, whether its orientation can be flipped, the primary colour mode, the rendering resolution and the preview mode

cards.name: Dribbble Shot large

It starts a document with a landscape page 800 x 600 px, aspect 4:3, RGB primary colour mode, 96 dpi rendering resolution and Enhanced view (the install file asks for 'Pixel Preview', which is not one of the app's view names (View > Normal, Enhanced, Pixels), and the app's own saved copy of the preset list holds Enhanced for this preset; switch to View > Pixels for pixel-exact work). It sets the page up only and has no look of its own; read from the install's PaperTypes.xml and DocDestinations.xml.
avoid: Treating the size as final: platforms change their image specs, so check the platform's current size before publishing; this preset is RGB at 96 dpi and not for print.
